provenance.review_tool: Claude Code (AI-assisted, directed by the maintainer)

reviewer_note: Static reading + 607 executed security tests; no repository modification.

findings.title: ToolSpec trust root is an HMAC key the authority runtime must hold; signing identities are labels
findings.claim_affected: PROV-02 ToolSpec; 'the deployment, not the agent, defines tool meaning' (DEVELOPER_OVERVIEW Q1)
findings.evidence: Bundle authenticity is HMAC-SHA256 under REMORA_TOOLSPEC_SIGNING_KEY. Strict profiles require that key in the authority process. With HMAC, the verifier can produce valid signatures. signing_identity is checked against a trusted/revoked allowlist, but all identities share one key, so revoking an identity does not stop a key holder from signing as another trusted identity. REMORA_TOOLSPEC_PINNED_DIGEST is optional and not a strict-profile prerequisite.
findings.scenario: Compromise of (or code execution in) the authority process yields the key; attacker re-signs a bundle that lowers risk_tier / changes action_type / widens targets for a destructive tool; PDP then ACCEPTs what it would have ESCALATEd. Every downstream binding faithfully binds the forged spec hash.
findings.mitigation: Strict profile, identity allowlist, optional pinned digest, lease binds toolspec_hash.
findings.insufficient: All mitigations trust the same key holder; pin is optional.
findings.minimal_fix: Make REMORA_TOOLSPEC_PINNED_DIGEST mandatory under review/controlled_pilot and record it in the audit chain at startup.
findings.architectural_fix: Ed25519 (or Sigstore) for bundles, signing offline/hardware; runtime holds only public keys per identity, so revocation of an identity revokes its key.
findings.required_test: A process holding only ToolSpec verification material cannot produce a bundle that loads; revoked identity's key is refused even when label is changed.

findings.title: PolicyDecisionToken is minted and consumed in the same function with a shared HMAC key
findings.claim_affected: PROV-05 PDP→PEP grant; README 'consumed once, at the policy-enforcement point'
findings.evidence: service.py issues the token and calls gate.check(..., consume=True) on the next lines in the same process; the gate verifies with the same REMORA_PDP_SIGNING_KEY. issuer is signed but never compared.
findings.scenario: Not an exploit by itself. The signature adds no separation: any code able to reach the gate can also mint tokens. Assurance readers may infer a PDP/PEP trust boundary that does not exist.
findings.mitigation: jti one-time ledger, context hash, audience, expiry are real and tested.
findings.insufficient: Separation of decision authority from enforcement is not established on this path.
findings.minimal_fix: Document the token as an in-process one-time grant record; compare issuer when configured.
findings.architectural_fix: Drop the token where PDP and PEP are co-located (the lease already carries grant_jti); keep a token only when it crosses a trust boundary, signed asymmetrically.
findings.required_test: Grant issued by a non-PDP key holder is refused by a PEP that holds only verification material.

findings.title: Tenant chosen by X-Remora-Tenant header in single-token mode outside development; review profile does not forbid it
findings.claim_affected: tenant isolation; tenant-scoped ledgers and chains
findings.evidence: In single-token mode the role header is ignored outside dev, but tenant is always taken from X-Remora-Tenant. The production guard requiring REMORA_API_TOKENS runs only for REMORA_ENV in {prod, production}. Any other value (staging, typo) is neither dev nor production. The strict 'review' profile requires neither the token table nor REMORA_ENV=production.
findings.scenario: A review deployment with REMORA_ENV=staging and one bearer token: any token holder reads/assesses/executes in any tenant by changing a header.
findings.mitigation: Documentation describes single-token as a dev/single-operator mode; controlled_pilot requires production env.
findings.insufficient: Mode is reachable under a strict profile; env value semantics are tri-state and inconsistent with the _get_env_mode docstring.
findings.minimal_fix: Under any non-dev env, single-token mode pins tenant to a configured value and refuses the header; review profile requires REMORA_API_TOKENS.
findings.architectural_fix: Single source of env truth (dev | production, refuse anything else); tenant always derived from credential.

findings.title: Separation of duties is role-only; admin can propose, approve and execute the same item
files: servers/api.py:1689 (_enforce_review_approval_role accepts admin for any approval_role)
findings.evidence: Approval checks role membership only; no comparison of approver principal with the proposing principal was found. admin holds assess, execute and review.
findings.scenario: One admin credential (or an agent operating with it) proposes a call, approves its own ESCALATE and executes it; the audit chain records a 'human' approval.
findings.mitigation: Operator role cannot review; tenant reviewer_roles can exclude admin if configured.
findings.insufficient: Default configuration permits self-approval by admin; not exploit-tested here.
findings.minimal_fix: Refuse approval when approver principal == proposer principal (record both in the item).
findings.architectural_fix: Two-person rule as a profile parameter; hardware-bound transaction approval (Phase 28).
findings.required_test: Same principal assess→approve → refused; distinct principals → allowed.

findings.title: Downstream-effect mediation is per-tool opt-in (mediated=False default), also under strict profiles
findings.evidence: register(tool, fn, mediated=False) by default; _prepare_mediation returns no mediator for unmediated tools; require_downstream_declaration applies only to mediated tools; effect-domain split is enabled only when REMORA_EFFECT_ENDPOINT is set.
findings.scenario: Authorized low-risk call on an unmediated tool reaches webhook/trigger/second-API effects with executor credentials; declared-delta verification ignores undeclared fields and can report EFFECT_VERIFIED.
findings.mitigation: DispatchResult reports mediated=False honestly; NTA-2 machinery exists.
findings.insufficient: Property is per-tool and per-deployment; no profile compels it.
findings.minimal_fix: Strict profiles refuse registration of unmediated tools unless the ToolSpec declares 'no downstream effects' and the executor holds no effect credentials.
findings.architectural_fix: Make the three-domain split (authority / tool code / effect) the strict-profile default.
findings.required_test: Strict profile + unmediated tool registration → refused; executor env without effect credentials asserted.

findings.title: Most lease bindings are configuration-conditional; outside strict profiles absence is logged, not refused
findings.claim_affected: DEVELOPER_OVERVIEW Q3 'Is authorization bound to the exact action? Yes'; PROV-03/04/16
findings.evidence: toolspec_hash checked only if bind_toolspec_identity; task identity only if supplied (require_task_identity default False); capability digest only if require_capability_set; resolved effect / runtime identity refused only under strict; surface in shadow by default; actor skipped if lease.actor_identity empty; audience skipped if gate has none. EnforcementGate.enforce() calls check without context and has no production caller.
findings.scenario: A library/reference deployment believes it has task/ToolSpec/capability binding because the lease signs those fields, while nothing compares them.
findings.mitigation: Strict profiles compel several; events are emitted; unbound-vs-mismatch reasons are distinct.
findings.insufficient: Claim text does not carry the conditions.
findings.minimal_fix: State bindings as a matrix of (binding × profile × resolver configured); remove or deprecate enforce().
findings.architectural_fix: Dispatcher construction takes a declared binding policy object and refuses to start if a required comparator is not bound.
findings.required_test: Per binding: strict profile without comparator → startup refusal.

findings.title: Audit chain signatures are HMAC and skipped when the verifier has no key; ≥6 chain implementations
findings.evidence: verify() only compares signatures when a key is present; key holders can forge; tail truncation needs an external head.
findings.scenario: An auditor without the key runs verify and reads 'intact' for a re-chained history.
findings.mitigation: Head row / expected_head; documentation says tamper-evident.
findings.insufficient: Verification result does not say 'signatures not checked'.
findings.minimal_fix: verify() returns signature_status: CHECKED | NOT_CHECKED_NO_KEY | UNSIGNED.
findings.architectural_fix: One chain implementation; asymmetric entry or checkpoint signatures; external anchoring of heads.
findings.required_test: Verifier without key reports NOT_CHECKED rather than intact.

findings.title: EFFECT_VERIFIED means 'accepted attestation of declared delta'; observer usually = executing deployment
findings.evidence: Module text is accurate. Undeclared fields are ignored by design; verifier is an allowlisted principal of the same deployment; verified_at and digests are verifier-supplied.
findings.scenario: External readers equate EFFECT_VERIFIED with independent confirmation that nothing else happened.
findings.mitigation: Honest docstrings; observation must postdate dispatch; uniqueness.
findings.insufficient: Status name is stronger than the claim.
findings.minimal_fix: Expose vantage (same_deployment | independent) and scope (declared_delta_only) on every receipt and report.
findings.required_test: Report generation cannot emit 'verified' without vantage and scope fields.

findings.title: Custody guard inspects declared environment-variable names only
findings.claim_affected: PROV-15 custody split as a hard guard; credential_non_bypassability
findings.evidence: Checks presence of names listed in REMORA_EFFECT_CREDENTIAL_ENV_NAMES and signing variables.
findings.scenario: IMDS/IAM role, workload identity, mounted secrets or undeclared env names give the authority process effect capability without tripping the guard.
findings.mitigation: README states REMORA cannot enforce against bypass credential paths.
findings.insufficient: Guard name implies more than it checks.
findings.architectural_fix: Deployment attestation of egress and identity (network policy, IAM deny) recorded as evidence.

findings.title: Paper TEE sentence equates attestation with 'correct model under the correct policy'
findings.evidence: 'the recorded decision is shown to have been produced by the correct model under the correct policy inside an isolated enclave'.
findings.insufficient: Attestation establishes workload identity/measurement, not correctness.
findings.minimal_fix: Replace with 'produced by a workload whose measurement matches the approved build and policy digest'.
findings.architectural_fix: AttestationEvidence as an EvidenceEnvelope subtype with does_not_establish: application_correctness.

findings.title: No signature domain separation; one HMAC key may sign both grants and leases
findings.evidence: Lease HMAC falls back to REMORA_PDP_SIGNING_KEY; both sign sorted compact JSON without a context prefix. Payload key sets are currently disjoint, so no concrete cross-type forgery was found.
findings.scenario: A future schema change makes a token payload parse as another object's preimage.
findings.mitigation: Typed reconstruction of payloads; disjoint fields.
findings.minimal_fix: Prefix every preimage with 'REMORA/<TYPE>/v<n>\0'; remove the key fallback.
findings.architectural_fix: Single signing service with mandatory domain tags.
findings.required_test: Signature over type A never verifies as type B with the same key.

findings.title: Concurrency test deadlocks on its failure path; full suite hangs on 1 vCPU
findings.evidence: If a writer future times out, stop.set() is never reached; 50 spinning readers keep the executor's shutdown(wait=True) blocked forever. Reproduced twice.
findings.scenario: On constrained runners the suite hangs instead of failing; a hang is easy to misread as infrastructure noise.
findings.architectural_fix: pytest-timeout in dev extras with a global ceiling.
findings.required_test: Test fails (not hangs) when writers are starved.

findings.title: Binding path is Python json.dumps, not RFC 8785; cross-language executors may diverge
findings.evidence: Float/large-int formatting differs between Python and JS; whether the TS mcp-gateway recomputes or re-serialises arguments was NOT_EVALUATED.
findings.scenario: authorize(Python value) then a JS executor sends a rounded integer or reformatted float.
findings.mitigation: Dispatcher rehash happens in Python before the call.
findings.insufficient: Downstream re-serialisation after rehash is unbound.
findings.minimal_fix: Restrict numeric arguments to safe-integer range and decimal strings in ToolSpec schemas.
findings.architectural_fix: exact-call-binding-v2 over RFC 8785 with golden vectors shared with foreign implementations.
findings.required_test: Golden vectors: Python and JS produce identical digests for the same JSON text.

findings.title: 963 KB benchmark dataset shipped as a Python module inside the production package
findings.evidence: Inline BoolQ-style data in a module under remora/.
findings.scenario: Increases wheel size and the surface reviewers must treat as code.
findings.minimal_fix: Move to data/ and load lazily.
findings.required_test: Release manifest excludes datasets from the runtime wheel.

findings.title: Grant ledger backends have different failure semantics
findings.evidence: D1 path converts outages into reason 'consumed_ledger_unavailable'; Postgres/SQLite catch only IntegrityError, so other DB errors propagate as exceptions (fail closed via 500, without a named reason in the chain).
findings.scenario: Operators cannot distinguish ledger outage from code fault on PG/SQLite.
findings.minimal_fix: Map OperationalError to a named refusal on all backends.
findings.architectural_fix: One ledger port with a typed Unavailable error.
findings.required_test: Simulated DB outage → refusal reason identical across backends.
